title: What an Airline Schedule Move Confers on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
An airline schedule notice recorded against a booking sold under Air Ticket Fare Brands is read against the fare brand held. These terms state what the carrier's records confer on the traveller.

**1. A move at or beyond the threshold of the brand held.** Such a move was formerly taken to give the traveller a right to be rebooked at no charge onto any flight the airline will accept, or to be refunded in full to the original form of payment whatever the brand's ordinary refund form. That basis is no longer in force.

**2. A move smaller than the threshold of the brand held.** Such a move was formerly taken to give no right, so that a traveller who still wished to move paid the disruption rebooking fee of the brand held, and a traveller who still wished to cancel was treated as a voluntary cancellation. That basis is no longer in force.

**3. Which notice decides.** Several notices on the same booking are not added together. The largest single move recorded on any one segment decides the right, and a notice later withdrawn by the airline is disregarded.

**4. A cancelled segment.** An airline cancellation of the segment is always treated as a move beyond the threshold, whatever its recorded minutes.

**5. An overnight stay.** Where the rebooking obliges the traveller to stay overnight, the overnight allowance of the brand held is reimbursed per traveller per night against a receipt. A brand carrying no allowance reimburses nothing.

**6. Repeated notices.** A booking that has received more than 3 notices in the last ninety days is passed to the disruption desk rather than rebooked again, because repeated moves indicate that the schedule itself is unstable. The count is of the disruption notices recorded against that booking, taken over the ninety days ending on the day the booking is considered, and a notice dated on the opening day of that span falls inside it. Both sides of the count: a booking carrying 3 such notices is not passed to the disruption desk, 3 not being more than 3, while a booking carrying 4 is. Worked on a hypothetical day of consideration of 17 September, the span opens on 20 June: a notice recorded on 20 June is counted, and a notice recorded on 19 June is not.
